tagline: Open benchmark index for EML expression encodings
hero_body:
This site curates Wolfram Language source expressions together with compiled EML strings for public comparison and reproducibility. Each source expression forms one group; multiple accepted encodings may appear under the same group to compare structural complexity.

The benchmark does not claim a unique globally minimal encoding or a single “correct” representation. Entries aim to be traceable and reviewable. If you have a strictly better construction or a correction, follow the submission workflow on this page.
section_board_desc:
The leaderboard is organized by source expression. When multiple accepted records exist for the same source, they are shown in one group for side-by-side comparison and review.

Rows whose verification label is seed (with baseline lineage) are the published reference baselines: their EML and metrics come from the original author’s reference compiler pipeline (eml_compiler_v4.py in SymbolicRegressionPackage; see Primer section 6). Labels such as pr, or pending with community lineage, mark community follow-up rows merged via pull request—you may see them next to the same source_wl to compare with the seed row.
baseline_catalog_desc: This block provides a coarse shape-based index for navigation before the detailed tables: literal constants, unary heads, binary operators, and a separate bucket for composite expressions. The split is a retrieval aid for human browsing only; it is not a formal taxonomy of function classes, equivalence classes, or semantics, and should not be read as a statement of problem difficulty or relative merit.
section_play_desc: This site is a static data view. A separate online compile service may be provided by maintainers in the future.
section_submit_example_caption: Save under submissions/incoming/ with a unique name (e.g. yourhandle_2026-04-26_log_example.json). The values above match the seed baseline for Log[x] on purpose; in your own PR you would typically propose a different eml, different metrics, and your own review notes. Run python3 scripts/validate_submissions.py before opening the pull request when possible.
section_submit_body:
End-to-end workflow from account setup to appearing on the public leaderboard. You do not need to run any backend service locally. **Do not edit public/data/leaderboard.json directly**; use the submissions folder so maintainers can review and then copy rows into the main dataset. A full JSON example is given below the step list.

1) Account and fork
Fork this repository and create a branch (e.g. feat/submission-handle).

2) Add a submission file (recommended)
In your fork, add **one JSON file per proposed row** under submissions/incoming/ (e.g. yourhandle_2026-04-21_sin_alt.json). Copy submissions/template.entry.json and fill every field. See submissions/README.md and docs/leaderboard.schema.json. For community rows, use lineage community and verified pending until maintainers update after review.

3) Field summary
• source_wl, eml, metrics as in the schema; metrics must match your toolchain output.
• lineage, verified, submitter: use values consistent with the template and schema (see this section and step 2).

4) Self-check
Run: python3 scripts/validate_submissions.py (validates JSON under submissions/incoming/).

5) Open a Pull Request
Title like submission: short summary; body describes verification and relation to existing rows.

6) Maintainer merge into the site
After the submission PR is accepted, maintainers **manually** append the row to public/data/leaderboard.json and deploy; they may move a copy to submissions/archive/ for traceability. The public page reflects the merged main table.

science_page_kicker: Scope definition for Elementary Meta-Language (EML) and this benchmark
science_s1_body:
In this project, Elementary Meta-Language (EML) refers to a string representation centered on the binary constructor EML[a,b], produced by a fixed compiler from Wolfram Language sources. The emphasis is on reproducibility: under a declared toolchain version, the mapping from source to EML is machine-checkable.

Grammar and reduction details are defined by the public EML toolchain this benchmark is aligned with; this page does not restate every rule. Different toolchain versions may yield different EML lengths for the same source, so comparisons should name the revision.
science_s2_body:
The dataset stores tuples of source expression, EML encoding, summary metrics, and provenance metadata (submitter and verification label). The intended use is similar to public benchmark tables: citeable rows for papers, implementations, or teaching.

Metrics describe structural features under stated definitions; they do not automatically imply mathematical superiority or global minimality. When citing the table, record the ordering policy and toolchain version to avoid misreading optimality claims.
science_s3_body:
Within one source group, rows follow a single ordering policy so on-screen ranks are comparable. The current policy sorts by maximum bracket nesting depth (ascending), then by EML node count (ascending).

This prioritizes shallower, smaller constructions under the chosen grammar; it does not replace symbolic minimality proofs. If the policy changes, it should be versioned alongside the dataset so historical comparisons remain interpretable.
science_s4_body:
Lineage distinguishes maintainer reference rows (baseline) from community submissions merged via pull request (community). Both may coexist under one source expression to compare reference constructions with community improvements.

In the last table column, the first line shows the submitter identifier; the second line states the verification label (for example seed or merged via PR). These labels describe process, not mathematical correctness by themselves.

The seed label in particular is explained in section 6: it ties those rows to the original author’s reference compile pipeline (eml_compiler_v4.py).
science_s5_body:
The public site reflects an accepted snapshot; upstream fixes or better encodings arrive through dataset updates and recorded revisions. For paper experiments, record the access date and the repository commit hash when available.

For stronger numerical or symbolic guarantees, rely on the formal validation path in the toolchain; this frontend publishes curated rows and welcomes corrections through the standard submission workflow.
science_s6_title: 6. Seed labels and the original reference toolchain
science_s6_body:
The verification label seed marks reference baseline rows. The EML string and summary metrics for each such row are produced by the original author’s public reference implement­ation: the Python compiler eml_compiler_v4.py in SymbolicRegressionPackage, applied to the Wolfram Language sources that define this benchmark (the declared constant, unary, and binary test forms, and the curated extended sources). The published values are the output of that compile step, not a hand-typed EML string for the same source.

In upstream work the seed table may be regenerated with the same pipeline (for example, compiling each listed source with eml_compiler_v4.py, as in a leaderboard generator), so the rows stay aligned with the published compiler and metrics definitions.
science_s6_repo_note: Source repository for eml_compiler_v4.py and the rest of the EML reference toolkit.
